tests.title: LoadSpec populates every artifact of a well-formed spec directory
given: a directory holding prd.md and the three JSON artifacts
tests.when: LoadSpec is called on that directory
then: Requirements, TestSpec and Tasks are all non-nil
tests.pseudocode: s, err = LoadSpec(dir); assert err == nil; assert s.Requirements != nil

tests.title: LoadSpec returns a LoadError naming the missing artifact
tests.when: LoadSpec is called on that directory
then: the error is a *LoadError whose File names requirements.json
tests.pseudocode: s, err = LoadSpec(dir); assert s == nil; assert errors.As(err, &LoadError{})

tests.title: Load then save is byte-identical for any well-formed spec
given: a corpus of well-formed spec directories
tests.when: for any spec in the corpus, it is loaded and saved to a fresh directory
then: each written file is byte-identical to the file it was read from
tests.pseudocode: for d in corpus: s = LoadSpec(d); s.Save(tmp); assert files_equal(d, tmp)

tests.title: Validate reports uncovered criteria and unowned tests
given: a spec whose second criterion is verified by no test
then: an error names the uncovered criterion
tests.pseudocode: r = spec.Validate(); assert not r.Valid; assert any(e.Check == 'C4' for e in r.Errors)

tests.title: A consumer loads and validates a spec end to end
tests.when: LoadSpec and Validate are called in sequence against the real filesystem
then: Validate reports the spec as valid
